hosted.gapReason: Hosted evidence is not exercised in this arm because deploying a new function bundle to the available shared development deployment is not safely namespace-isolated. The official anonymous local deployment is used instead; this is not scored as a product failure.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: The admin-proof authoritative query sees four lists of 25 tasks, exactly 100 task rows, and exactly two active members; three stable Convex Auth user hashes are retained.
Independent Alice and Bob Convex Auth browser profiles each received all 100 authorized tasks from the reactive query.
Mallory remained a stable authenticated Convex Auth user but received zero protected tasks and no workspace lists.
scenarioResults.note: Authorization was enforced inside the reactive backend query.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Two independent member clients observed create, edit, complete, reopen, reorder, and delete mutations; the final admin-proof summary returned to exactly 100 tasks.
scenarioResults.note: Convex mutations supplied the transaction and settlement boundary.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Bob observed Alice's committed insert and delete without refresh over a directly observed WebSocket connection to the local Convex backend.

scenarioResults.note: GAP: a warm connected page retained 100 in-memory rows during transport loss, but closing and reopening the previously used profile while the backend was unavailable produced no authenticated app shell and zero retained rows.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: With the exact local backend process paused, the warm client accepted one create and one update while its remote task count stayed 100; both calls remained pending for reconnect.
scenarioResults.note: The form/input state supplied local UI evidence; Convex retained the mutation calls in the warm session.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: After the exact backend resumed, both offline calls settled, the new title appeared, exactly one created marker existed, the count became 101, and cleanup returned the authoritative count to 100.
A two-client barrier issued concurrent title mutations; an independent admin-proof query identified the committed winner and both clients converged to it.
scenarioResults.note: Policy: serializable optimistic concurrency with the last committed mutation visible.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Concurrent mutations changed one list-owned task ID sequence; the subscribed client derived exactly the unique positions 0 through 24.
Convex Auth logout removed the protected query result; automatic anonymous sign-in created a different unprivileged user with zero protected tasks.
Deactivating Bob's membership while connected cleared his protected query, and Alice's subsequent marker was not delivered until Bob was explicitly regranted.
The retained receipt contains two warmups and seven raw local samples for admin CLI read, mutation-to-origin, second-client push, browser reopen/resubscribe, and production client build.
scenarioResults.note: Small frozen local profile only; the CLI read includes process startup and these are not production-scale claims.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: The post-cleanup probe found all three exact arm listeners closed and the local deployment, browser runtime, environment file, and proof file absent.
scenarioResults.note: No shared Convex deployment was modified.

glue: admin-proof CLI bridge for seed, membership, and authoritative reads
persistent-browser persona provisioner with stale-membership repair
two-client browser correctness, offline, and performance barriers

actor-authority.reason: Three stable Convex Auth users were exercised positively and negatively, including connected revocation and logout.

transaction-conflict.reason: Two-client barriers and an independent admin-proof query directly proved the serialized conflict winner and ordering invariant.

transport.reason: Independent browser clients opened native Convex WebSockets and retained raw second-client push samples.

offline-reconnect.reason: A process-level transport barrier directly distinguished warm cache retention, the cold-boot GAP, queued warm mutations, and reconnect.

settlement.reason: Online and offline mutations were observed before and after authority, with exactly-one marker and an authoritative count after settlement.

target-identity.reason: The exact anonymous local deployment was hashed, queried authoritatively, and bound to the cleanup receipt.

cleanup-isolation.reason: The predeclared plan guarded process ownership and proved all listeners, runtime state, and ignored credentials absent.

artifact-reproducibility.reason: Source, deterministic seed, generated APIs, production build, and category-separated inventory are retained.

cleanup.postCleanupProbe: Ports 3210, 3211, and 4179 were closed; the exact local deployment, browser runtime, environment file, and admin-proof file were absent.
